newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open up, edge lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open up, edge lower in quiet trade.

text.p: French stocks opened slightly higher on Monday but then slipped into negative territory in quiet trading.
"With New York closed today (for the U.S. Labor Day holiday), it's very calm and likely to stay that way," said one trader.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 0.81 point or 0.04 percent at 1,969.80 at 0850 GMT, while the CAC-40 September futures contract was up one point at 1,974.

Traders said the bourse, which has closed down for the past five sessions, will probably trade in a narrow range ahead of the U.S. August jobs report due out on Friday and the French 1997 budget due out on September 10.

Euro Disney rallied more than four percent after Chairman Philippe Bourguignon told a newspaper that the company was on track to show a second annual profit for the year ending on September 30 after a "satisfying" summer.
